title: Permission matrix fuzzing and audit-replay regression harness
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: build a robust regression harness that combines permission-matrix fuzzing, deterministic policy snapshotting, and audit-log replay to catch RBAC v2 regressions across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. The harness will exercise role collisions, inherited permissions, SSO/SAML federated assertions, and admin-level escalation paths. It must be deterministic for CI snapshots while still exposing nondeterministic edge cases via a nightly stochastic run.

Scope:
- Permission matrix fuzzing engine that synthesizes realistic role/actor/policy trees and produces expected allow/deny outcomes (policy oracle).
- Canonical snapshot store (policy mosaics) that are versioned and used as regression baselines.
- Audit-replay runner that consumes real sanitized audit logs from staging and replays them against current RBAC engine codepaths to detect behavioral drift.
- SAML/SSO integration shim to validate assertion-derived attributes and session bindings under synthetic and recorded flows.
- CI integration: unit + deterministic integration tests on PR, nightly stochastic fuzzing + audit-replay job with coverage/health dashboards.

Approach and decisions made so far:
- Chose a hybrid fuzzing model: structural generator (role graphs + permission combinators) + mutation stage to simulate admin misconfigurations. Structural generator ensures coverage of common topologies; mutation finds collision edge cases.
- Policy oracle design: using a small reference interpreter (policy-sim) running in the test harness to compute ground-truth outcomes instead of relying on live runtime snapshots. This avoids flakiness when the runtime is changing during development.
- Snapshot format: JSONL canonical mosaics with salted but reversible entity IDs to maintain reproducibility across runs and allow human inspection. Snapshots will live in the repo under /test-fixtures/policy-mosaics/ and be signed with a CI key to prevent accidental mutation.
- Audit replay: sanitize logs in staging via the audit-sanitizer tool (removes PII, tokens) then convert into replayable events. Replays will run against a stubbed identity provider for SAML to avoid external network dependence.

Trade-offs and reasons:
- Deterministic PR checks limited to small, representative mosaics to keep runtime low; larger combinatorial mosaics reserved for nightly runs to balance CI costs.
- Using a reference policy interpreter increases maintenance but gives a stable ground truth for regression detection; long-term plan is to upstream parts of the interpreter into the runtime for parity checks.

Artifacts and links:

- Prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6742 (perm-matrix-fuzzer)
- Test fixtures: repo path: /test-fixtures/policy-mosaics/
- CI jobs: ci/rbac/perm-matrix-pr-check, ci/rbac/perm-matrix-nightly, ci/rbac/audit-replay-nightly
- Dashboard: internal Grafana: dashboard/d-sQ2x-perm-matrix-fuzzing (coverage + flaky test rate)

2025-02-27 - Blocker: SAML staging IDP occasionally returns clock-skewed assertions causing replay flakiness. Proposed mitigation: canonicalize timestamps in audit-sanitizer and stub NTP for CI containers.
2025-03-01 - Decision: Nightly stochastic runs will be limited to 25k synthetic events to control cost; we will increase if coverage/defect signal justifies it.
2025-03-03 - Rafael pushed fix for reversible ID salting and added snapshot signing step; need infra to store CI signing key in k8s secret manager. Assigned infra ticket INF-994 for key provisioning.
